correctness.rationale: The exponent separation in (x^-1+1+x)^(5m+t) modulo 5 is exact for 0<=t<=4: a term from the low digit has exponent of absolute value at most four, so it cannot cancel a nonzero multiple of five. The group-ring digit distribution is (1+J)^R=1+(5^R-1)J/4. In the histogram of exponent pairs (S(m),S(m+1)-S(m)), a low digit a<4 contributes A_R(s-e(a)) when d=a; the low digit 4 contributes B_R(s-2,d+2) to B_{R+1}(s,d). Unrolling, with B_0 concentrated at (0,0), gives the displayed formula including the all-four carry into a new digit. The five final-digit cases then give exactly N_r, with B_R=5^R/16+O(R+1) and the claimed rational masses. The three no-carry sets are disjoint (b-a=0,1,2 and c!=b), and the two carry sets b=a-1 and c=b intersect in four cells. The low digit plus one free high digit realizes every pair (s,d), so the support is already full at 125 starts. For arbitrary N the base-five aligned blocks translate the exponents diagonally except at at most two boundary starts per block; P is translation-invariant, and at most four blocks per depth each cost O(r+1), proving the log-squared error. An independent replay, python3 /workspace/audit_trinomial.py, used repeated Laurent-polynomial multiplication and a digit-pair histogram recursion rather than the supplied checker. It matched all triple counts at depths 1–5 (support sizes 5,22,40,40,40), the limiting tiers and both adjacent-pair and lag-two checks. The all-depth result is deductive, not inferred from finite checks. The scope's modular-arithmetic wording should be read as applying to exponent operations and indicator arguments, not sums of counts or rational probabilities.
